<thought>To fulfill the task, I will retrieve polymorphs for a diverse set of sulphide compositions (up to the allowed 40) using the batch tool with the given energy and count limits, then consolidate all resulting JSON files into a single dataset and report its path.</thought>
<action>batch_retrieve_polymorphs</action>
<action_input>{
    "compositions": [
        "FeS", "FeS2", "CuS", "Cu2S", "ZnS", "PbS", "CdS", "MoS2", "WS2",
        "NiS", "Ni3S2", "CoS", "Co9S8", "SnS", "SnS2", "Bi2S3", "Sb2S3",
        "Ag2S", "AgS", "Ga2S3", "In2S3", "Al2S3", "SiS2", "TiS2", "V2S3",
        "Cr2S3", "MnS", "MnS2", "PtS", "PdS", "Au2S", "AuS", "GeS",
        "GeS2", "HgS"
    ],
    "max_energy_above_hull": 0.3,
    "max_per_composition": 3,
    "save_directory": "sulphide_polymorphs"
}</action_input>
